subject: Interim IR notification: afternoon token drift — request for IRP & evidence bundle
messages:
From: John Miller <jmiller@finsecure.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@finsecure.com
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unusual API token refreshes observed — initial heads-up

Hi Marissa,

We noticed a spike in token refresh activity tied to our account between 08:40–08:55 PDT (see attached summaries). Nothing appears to be malicious from our side yet, but compliance needs an interim summary and a copy of your Incident Response Plan that covers access token compromise scenarios. Can you send an outline of the IR steps you followed and any artifacts (sanitized logs, notification timeline) you can share quickly?

We need this to feed our internal SOC review and procurement is waiting before they approve the next contract milestone.

Thanks,
John Miller
Security Operations, FinSecure Bank

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: John Miller <jmiller@finsecure.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unusual API token refreshes observed — initial heads-up

John — thanks for flagging and for the detail. We see a brief elevated refresh rate originating from a background-job shard in our hosted runtime; we classified this as a "token drift" event while we confirm root cause.

Immediate next steps from Redwood's side (executed):
- Scoped and throttled the affected shard (09:02 PDT).
- Rotated the short-lived keys tied to that shard and cleared active sessions for impacted tokens (09:08 PDT).
- Gathered request logs and rotated sampling export ready for redaction (09:16 PDT).

Deliverables we will send within the hour:
1) Redacted timeline and postmortem summary (PDF) — includes mitigations and headcount on-call chronology.
2) Request log export (ZIP) containing token-level timestamps and request metadata (sanitized).
3) Snapshot of the IRP section relevant to token compromise (PDF) and contact list CSV for your SOC contact.

I will also include the specific control mappings to SOC 2 CC6 and SIG entries related to session management. If you have any additional format requests for the artifacts, let me know.

Marissa Cole
Director, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 10:01:23 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unusual API token refreshes observed — internal coordination

Marissa — attaching the PR timeline and the raw sampling we took from the runtime. Ben and I already removed the problematic background worker and pushed a soft fix to the autoscaler to prevent rapid re-spawning. Notes:
- Root cause: edge-case race during lease renewal under sustained ephemeral load (rare timing window).
- No evidence of credential exfiltration; refreshes were internal to our process and the refreshed tokens were short-lived.

Ben, can you package the raw logs and the redaction checklist for delivery? Neha, please prep the SOC2 mapping doc and a short statement confirming control CC6 was not bypassed.

--Karthik

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: John Miller <jmiller@finsecure.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Deliverables: redacted logs, IR summary, SOC2 mapping

John — attaching the artifacts (delivery stub below). Per Marissa's note, these are redacted to remove internal PII and tenant-scoped identifiers. Full file transfer is via our secure drive link; password will be shared over the phone on request.

Attachment stubs: request_log_export_20260609.zip (sanitized CSVs), redacted_postmortem_v1.pdf (concise timeline + root cause + remediation), IRP_summary_contact_list.csv

Summary highlights:
- Event window: 08:40–08:55 PDT, affected subset ~0.4% of token refreshes
- Action: throttled, rotated, removed faulty worker, deployed autoscaler guard (09:02–09:20 PDT)
- Impact: no customer data exfiltration detected; transient increase in latency for <0.1% of requests
- Follow-ups: post-deploy monitoring for 72 hours and a change to our canary checks to include renewal-path scenarios

Link to artifacts: https://drive.redwood.internal/secure/FinSecure-IRP-20260609

If procurement needs a formal SOC2 attestation excerpt, loop Neha and I will attach the control extract.

Ben Carter
Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: John Miller <jmiller@finsecure.com>, procurement@finsecure.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: redacted postmortem and IRP excerpt delivered

John / Procurement team — closing the loop on today's token drift event. Attached is the redacted postmortem (redacted_postmortem_v1.pdf), sanitized request logs (request_log_export_20260609.zip), and a short IRP excerpt mapping to SOC2 CC6.

Key ask from FinSecure for ongoing compliance: please confirm receipt and whether you require further redaction or a limited NDA addendum for the full telemetry set. If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute walk-through with our on-call engineers to go through the timeline and controls.

Thanks for the quick collaboration — we appreciate the partnership and the extra diligence on procurement side while you review the artifacts.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Trust & Security | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0182

[Forwarded/Included files]
- request_log_export_20260609.zip (attachment stub; sanitized CSVs)
- redacted_postmortem_v1.pdf (attachment stub; timeline + root cause + mitigation steps)
- IRP_summary_contact_list.csv (attachment stub; escalations and on-call numbers)
